'''Yonggom''' is one of the [[Ok languages]] of [[Indonesia]] and [[Papua New Guinea]]. According to its speakers, it is part of a continuum of 9 mutually intelligible dialects of [[Muyu language]]s which also includes Muyu, North Muyu (Kadi), South Muyu, and [[Ninggerum language|Ningrum]].<ref name='zahrer'>Zahrer, Alexander. 2019. ''First data of Moyu, a lowland Ok language of New Guinea''. 11th International Austronesian and Papuan Languages and Linguistics Conference ([https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/binaries/content/assets/geesteswetenschappen/leiden-university-centre-for-linguistics/apll11-booklet-of-abstracts-2019-06-05.pdf APLL11] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221216024813/https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/binaries/content/assets/geesteswetenschappen/leiden-university-centre-for-linguistics/apll11-booklet-of-abstracts-2019-06-05.pdf |date=2022-12-16 }}), 13-15 Juni 2019, [[Universitas Leiden]].</ref> Petabahasa by [[Indonesian Ministry of Education]] classified this language as ''Yonggom/Yongkom'' <small>(BPS:1158 6)</small> spoken in Kampung Ninati,<ref name="yonggom">{{cite web | title=Yonggom | website=Peta Bahasa | url=https://petabahasa.kemdikbud.go.id/infopencarian.php?idb=738 | language=id | access-date=2024-10-12 | archive-date=2025-08-13 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250813092002/https://petabahasa.kemdikbud.go.id/infopencarian.php?idb=738 | url-status=dead }}</ref> although another name recorded for ''South Muyu'' <small>(BPS:0917 2)</small> is ''Yongon''.<ref name="Musl">{{cite web | title=Muyu Selatan | website=Peta Bahasa | url=https://petabahasa.kemdikbud.go.id/infobahasa.php?idb=539 | language=id | access-date=2024-10-12 | archive-date=2024-02-29 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229093439/https://petabahasa.kemdikbud.go.id/infobahasa.php?idb=539 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://id.scribd.com/doc/265465163/Master-Bahasa|title=Master Bahasa BPS 2010|website=Scribd|language=id|access-date=2020-07-06}}</ref>

* /b, d/ can become fricatives [β, ð] intervocalically in fast speech.
* /k/ can be heard as a fricative [ɣ] in fast speech.
* /ɾ/ becomes [l] in word-initial position.
* /j/ is heard as an affricate [dʒ] when following a plosive.
